slides.texte_overlay:
how to become the person who
knows a little about everything

follow every rabbit hole

when something makes you curious, give it ten minutes right then. the people who know a bit about everything are simply the ones who never ignore their own questions.

mix your sources

read a science article, listen to a history podcast and watch an art video in the same week. variety is what turns scattered facts into a mind that connects everything.

teach it back

after you learn something, explain it to a friend that same day. saying it out loud locks it in your memory, and you instantly find out what you didn't really understand.

one lesson a day

spend 5 minutes a day on one short lesson in a completely different subject each time. a year of tiny lessons covers more ground than most people cover in a whole degree.
slides.texte_sophia:

spend 5 minutes a day on one short lesson in a new subject each time. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, and a year of tiny lessons covers a huge amount.

slides.texte_overlay:
keep a learned list

write down one thing you learned every day in a small notebook. after a few months, scrolling back through that list is the best proof that you're getting smarter.
